The speaker announced a tax cut for small businesses, reducing the company tax rate to 28.5% for incorporated businesses with turnover under $2 million from 1 July 2015, claiming it is the lowest rate since 1967 and the largest small business package in Australian history.
The bills introduce a 28.5% tax rate for small businesses with turnover under $2 million and an immediate tax deduction for eligible assets under $20,000 each.

The speaker supported the Tax Laws Amendment (Small Business Measures No. 1 and 2) Bills 2015, which cut the company tax rate to 28.5% for small businesses and introduced $20,000 accelerated depreciation, but argued the government's public service job cuts had severely damaged Canberra’s economy, citing a 41% drop in building approvals and the lowest business confidence in Australia.

Labor supported the two small business tax bills, including the 1.5 per cent company tax cut and $20,000 accelerated depreciation, but criticised the government for blocking Labor's immediate attempt to pass them despite urging urgency. The speaker referenced Bill Shorten's support and Tony Abbott's call to pass the bill straightaway.

The coalition's $5.5 billion Growing Jobs and Small Business package reduces the company tax rate to 28.5% for businesses with turnover under $2 million and increases the instant asset write-off threshold to $20,000. It also provides accelerated depreciation for primary producers on fencing, water facilities, and fodder storage.

The member for Lyne announced the bills deliver a 1.5 per cent company tax cut for incorporated small businesses with turnover under $2 million, applying retrospectively, and a five per cent tax benefit, arguing the measures provide concrete help to small businesses.

The speaker thanked 31 members (16 coalition, 15 opposition) for debating small business interests representing 300,000 small businesses. The bills lower the company tax rate to 28.5% for 780,000 small businesses, expand asset write-offs from $1,000 to $20,000, and allow farmers immediate deductions for fencing, water facilities, and fodder storage, effective from 12 May 2015.
